newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - Factors to watch - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - Factors to watch - April 15.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Tuesday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* Market is seen as generally weak but pockets of technical support may be seen in reaction to the Dow's overnight uptick, Lawrence de Leon, analyst at Dharmala Securities Phils Inc said.
* Sun Hung Kai Securities said in its daily outlook that the market will look towards New York for direction.
* BPI Securities Corp analyst Roberto Cano said investors should consider banking and property issues which have experienced heavy profit-taking in recent days.
* On Monday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index fell 43.94 points to 2,932.84.
* On Monday, the Dow Jones rose 60.21 points to 6,451.90. PLDT's ADR shed $0 1/2 to $58 1/2.

* Benpres Holdings Corp said its board decided to recommend to stockholders the transfer of its shares in ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp and SkyVision Corp to Lopez Inc in exchange for a convertible instrument.
* Dealers of Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp cut prices of diesel and unleaded gasoline on Monday by 10 centavos per litre each.

* Newspaper Philippine Star said 13 groups filed with the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) on Monday their opposition to the application of PLDT for "rate rebalancing" saying they were not against the proposed metering system that was part of the "rebalancing" but were questioning the amount PLDT wanted to impose.

* Philippine Daily Inquirer quoting a company source saying the merger deal between Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc and Coca-Cola Amatil did not get the full support of the 15-member board of San Miguel Corp. The deal is expected to take centre stage in San Miguel's stockholders meeting today.
* The Philippine benchmark 91-day treasury bill rate rose by an average of 10.107 percent at the regular weekly auction on Monday from 9.583 percent last week.
* The peso closed higher at 26.362 to the dollar vs 26.363.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.03125 percent.
